answer.rationale: Temporal structure points at the release: deploy 2h ago, degradation began ~90m ago, and the blast radius is confined to the primary region where the build landed. That makes the release the leading candidate cause, and rollback is the only option that addresses a cause rather than redistributing load around it. I am verifying memory_b1 and memory_b2 because they are the two contenders and both are recorded as outcome-only successes with no record of the conditions that made them work. For b1 I need to know whether the day-18 rollback was during comparable write-heavy peak load and whether the prior build was verified good or merely assumed good. For b2 I need to know whether the March failover carried in-flight writes cleanly or whether write loss was simply not measured — 'error rates recovered within minutes' says nothing about durability, and with settlement traffic at daily peak a failover with replication lag is the one path that can directly violate the primary objective of not losing customer writes. Rejecting the others: add_capacity (b3) treats a saturation pattern that a region-confined post-deploy regression does not match; circuit breakers (b4) fit a failing external dependency, and the write path here is degrading, not erroring out; read-replica routing (b5) relieved read pressure from dashboards, which is not the load profile at settlement peak. Scale is deliberately a small guarded test: revert on a bounded slice of primary-region write traffic with drain-then-cut, per the staged-gating pattern in b6, so that if p99 does not respond within a short window I have learned the release is not the cause and have not spent the single intervention on a full-fleet change. Explicit uncertainty: the release-to-onset correlation is suggestive, not established; a coincident settlement-volume record or a slow resource leak predating the deploy would produce the same signature. Downstream risk flagged: every inherited memory here records only what worked, with no failure or near-miss entries, so the corpus is survivorship-biased and its apparent reliability is partly an artifact of what got written down. Whatever I do today will be consolidated as another success story and will bias the next session toward this action under conditions that may not match. I am therefore recording the causal hypothesis, the guard conditions, the load profile, and the negative result if the rollback does not help — not just the outcome.
